question: A convex mirror is made from a part of the surface of a sphere of radius 10.0 cm. Its principal focus will be at a distance of .......... from its pole.
solution:
The correct answer is __**5.0 cm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The principal focus of a convex mirror is located at a distance of half the radius of curvature from its pole.
 
• Given that the radius of curvature of the convex mirror is 10.0 cm, the principal focus will be at a distance of **5.0 cm** from the pole.
 
• In a convex mirror, the principal focus is virtual and lies behind the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The formula for the focal length (f) of a mirror is given by f=R2" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f=R2f=R2" id="MathJax-Element-58-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f=R2f=R2" id="MathJax-Element-45-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f=R2f=R2 f=R2 f=R2 f=R2 f = \frac{R}{2} , where R is the radius of curvature.
 
• For convex mirrors, the focal length is considered positive, while for concave mirrors, it is negative.
 
• Convex mirrors are commonly used for rearview mirrors in vehicles because they provide a wider field of view.
